mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a risk premium adjustment that drives positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not outperform a 5-day rolling average by more than 0.5% in 60 out of 100 triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS labor cost index above the prior quarter's median is associated with tighter labor market conditions that precede negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > Q1 2017 median for the current month
failure_condition: Over 80% of such events result in non-negative 60-day forward returns, or the 5-year average IC is not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in GDPC1 personal consumption exceeding 2% signals weakening demand, which predicts negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by >2% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: More than 70% of such events produce non-negative 20-day returns, or the 12-month moving average of IC is not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in INDPRO manufacturing index below 95 triggers a supply-side shock that produces positive S&P 20-day forward returns as market anticipates profit reallocation.
failure_condition: Over 50% of such events fail to deliver positive 20-day returns, or the 3-month average IC change is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in a single month, the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to turn negative due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: More than 60% of such events result in non-negative 60-day returns, or the 12-month average IC is not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both PAYEMS and UNRATE below their 2016 Q4 medians indicates labor market softening and wage moderation, predicting positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 2016 Q4 median AND UNRATE < 2016 Q4 median
failure_condition: The combined signal is active in >30% of months but produces non-positive 20-day returns in >70% of those months (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of sustained monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 1.5%), a 5-day drop in HOUST housing starts followed by a 5-day rise predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates recovery.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1.5% AND HOUST drops for 5 consecutive days then rises in next 5 days
failure_condition: The pattern occurs 10 times but only results in positive returns 2 times (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS demand for financial assets falls by more than 5% in a month, it indicates excess liquidity and a subsequent negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors reallocate to safer assets.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >5% in the current month
failure_condition: Over 80% of such events produce non-negative 60-day returns, or the 6-month moving average of RSAFS is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.1).
